title: What Does Hard-Negative Fine-Tuning Teach Multimodal Large Language Models? Controlled Evidence from a Compositional Benchmark
abstract: arXiv:2611.18701v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Fine-tuning on hard negatives is a popular way to improve the compositional reasoning of vision-language models, but when accuracy goes up it is rarely clear what the model actually learned. We ask this question for multimodal large language models. We use CompHall, 2,860 forced-choice questions (spatial, attribute, counting and part-whole) with two graded hard negatives each, three model families (LLaVA-1.5, LLaVA-NeXT and Idefics2), and controls that such studies often lack: gray-image evaluation, three seeds, option-order tests, control arms trained on different question types, and independent benchmarks. We find four things. First, CompHall is not a pure test of vision: part-whole questions can be answered from the text alone (66-95% without the image), and per-image accuracy is unrelated to an object-hallucination probe (r = -0.05), so we see no evidence that compositional failures drive hallucination. translated_title: 硬负样本微调教会了多模态大语言模型什么？来自组合性基准的受控证据
translated_abstract: 在硬负样本上进行微调是提升视觉-语言模型组合推理能力的一种流行方法，但当准确率上升时，模型究竟学到了什么往往并不清楚。我们针对多模态大语言模型提出了这一问题。我们使用CompHall基准——包含2,860道强制选择题（涵盖空间、属性、计数和部分-整体关系），每题配有两个分级硬负样本——以及三个模型家族（LLaVA-1.5、LLaVA-NeXT和Idefics2），并加入了此类研究通常缺乏的对照手段：灰度图像评估、三个随机种子、选项顺序测试、在不同题型上训练的对照组，以及独立基准测试。我们发现了四点。第一，CompHall并非纯粹的视觉测试：部分-整体问题仅凭文本即可回答（无图像时准确率为66-95%），且逐图像准确率与物体幻觉探测无关（r = -0.05），因此我们没有发现组合推理失败会驱动幻觉的证据。第二，原始的微调……
tldr: 本文通过CompHall基准及多种严格对照实验，探究多模态大语言模型从硬负样本微调中真正学到了什么，发现部分-整体问题仅凭文本即可作答，且组合推理失败与物体幻觉之间并无关联。
en_tdlr: Using the CompHall benchmark with rigorous controls, this paper investigates what multimodal LLMs actually learn from hard-negative fine-tuning, finding that part-whole questions can be answered from text alone and that compositional failures do not drive object hallucination.
